claim: Among nonempty finite ultrametric spaces, the full verbose Vietoris–Rips barcode over a fixed coefficient field determines the isometry class whenever the cardinality is at most four; a published five-point ultrametric pair has identical verbose barcodes but is not isometric, so five is the minimum cardinality at which this invariant fails to determine isometry.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity: Restricted to nonempty finite ultrametric spaces and the full verbose Vietoris–Rips barcode over a fixed coefficient field. The five-point counterexample is attributed to Mémoli–Zhou; the lower-bound classification for at most four points is proved explicitly. Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
title: The five-point threshold for verbose Vietoris–Rips barcode rigidity on ultrametrics
